1272.subject: Physics
1272.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
1272.text: A neutron makes a head-on elastic collision with a stationary deuteron. The fractional energy loss of the neutron in the collision is
1272.sol: One deuteron consists of one proton and one neutron. As the mass of a proton and a neutron is approximately same $\left(\approx 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~kg}\right)$, we assume that the mass of the neutron be $m$ and the mass of the deuteron be $2 m$ as the electron mass is negligibly small compared to that of proton and neutron. Let the initial velocity of the neutron be $u$. As the deuteron is initially at rest, the final velocity of the neutron is v_1=$\left(\frac{m-2 m}{m+2 m}\right)$u=-$\frac{m u}{3 m}=-\frac{u}{3} .$and the velocity of the deuteron is v_2=$\frac{2 m}{m+2 m}$u=$\frac{2}{3}$u $\text{. }$Total energy before collision is $E_1=\frac{1}{2} m u^2$ After collision, the energy gained by the deuteron is E_d=$\frac{1}{2} \times($2 m) v_2^2=m $\times\left(\frac{2}{3}$u\right)^2=$\frac{4}{9}$m u² . $E_d$ is the amount of energy lost by the neutron. Therefore the fractional loss of energy of the neutron is $\frac{E_d}{E_1}=\frac{(4 / 9) m u^2}{(1 / 2) m u^2}=\frac{8}{9}$

7007.text: If one of the two circle \(x²+y²+\alpha_1(x-y)+c=0\) and \(x²+y²+\alpha_2(x-y)+c=0\), lies within the other, then (where \(\alpha_1, \alpha_2 \in \mathbf{R}, \alpha_1 \neq \alpha_2\))
7007.sol:
Equation of given circles are
$$\begin{aligned}& x²+y²+\alpha_1(x-y)+C=0 \\
& \text{and }x^2+y²+\alpha_2(x-y)+C=0
\end{aligned}$$\)
Since, if one of the two given circles, lies within the other, then
$C_1 C_2  <  \left|r_1-r_2\right|\)
\begin{array}{ll}\text{Where, }& C_1=\left(\frac{-\alpha_1}{2}, \frac{-\alpha_1}{2}\right),C_2=\left(\frac{-\alpha_2}{2}, \frac{-\alpha_2}{2}\right)\\
& r_1=\sqrt{\frac{\alpha_1^2}{2}-C} \text{ and }r_2=\sqrt{\frac{\alpha_2^2}{2}-C}\\
\therefore & \sqrt{\frac{\left(\alpha_1-\alpha_2\right)^2}{2}} <  \left|\sqrt{\frac{\alpha_1^2}{2}-C}-\sqrt{\frac{\alpha_2^2}{2}-C}\right|
\end{array}$
\(\Rightarrow \frac{\alpha_1^2+\alpha_2^2-2 \alpha_1 a_2}{2} <  \left(\frac{\alpha_1^2}{2}-C\right) +\left(\frac{\alpha_2^2}{2}-C\right) -2 \sqrt{\frac{\alpha_1^2}{2}-C} \sqrt{\frac{\alpha_2^2}{2}-C}\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad-\alpha_1 \alpha_2 <  -2 C-\sqrt{\alpha_1^2-2 C} \sqrt{\alpha_2^2-2 C}\)
\(\Rightarrow \quad\left(\alpha_1^2-2 C\right)\left(\alpha_2^2-2 C\right) <  \left(\alpha_1 \alpha_2-2 C\right)^2\)
\(\Rightarrow \alpha_1^2 \alpha_2^2-2\left(\alpha_1^2+\alpha_2^2\right) C+4 C² <  \alpha_1^2 \alpha_2^2-4 C \alpha_1 \alpha_2+4 C²\)
\(\Rightarrow 2 C\left[\alpha_1^2+\alpha_2^2-2 \alpha_1 \alpha_2\right]  >  0\)
\(\Rightarrow C\left(\alpha_1-\alpha_2\right)^2  >  0 \Rightarrow C  >  0\) as \(\alpha_1 \neq \alpha_2\)
Hence, option (c) is correct.

7044.subject: Mathematics
7044.text: The equation of a circle passing through the points of intersection of the circles $x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x - 6y - 12 = 0, x^{2} + y^{2} + 6x + 4y - 12 = 0$ and having radius $\sqrt{13} is$
7044.sol:
The equation of a circle passing through the points of
intersection of the circles,

$\left(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x - 6x - 12\right) + \lambda\left(x^{2} + y^{2} + 6x + 4y - 12\right) = 0$

$x^{2} ( 1 + \lambda ) + y^{2} ( 1 + \lambda ) + x ( 6\lambda - 4 ) + y ( 4\lambda - 6 ) - 12\lambda - 12 = 0$

$\text{Rewrite$ the above equation.}

$x^{2} + y^{2} + \dfrac{x ( 6\lambda - 4 )}{( 1 + \lambda )} + \dfrac{y ( 4\lambda - 6 )}{( 1 + \lambda )} - 12 = 0$

$\text{On comparing$ in equations with}x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0

$g = \dfrac{( 3\lambda - 2 )}{( 1 + \lambda )}, f = \dfrac{( 2\lambda - 3 )}{( 1 + \lambda )}, c = - 12$

$\text{It is given that$ the $radius is}\sqrt{13}$

$13 = \dfrac{( 3\lambda - 2{)}^{2}}{( 1 + \lambda{)}^{2}} + \dfrac{( 2\lambda - 3{)}^{2}}{( 1 + \lambda{)}^{2}} + 12$

$13 ( 1 + \lambda{)}^{2} = ( 3\lambda - 2{)}^{2} + ( 2\lambda - 3{)}^{2} + 12 ( 1 + \lambda{)}^{2}$

$\text{After simplification,}$

$13{λ}^{2} + 13 + 26\lambda = 25{λ}^{2} + 25$

$12{λ}^{2} - 26\lambda + 12 = 0$

$6{λ}^{2} - 13\lambda + 6 = 0$

$( 2\lambda - 3 ) ( 3\lambda - 2 ) = 0$

$\lambda = \dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\text{The required equation when}\lambda = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$x^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{2}\right) + y^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{2}\right) + x\left(6 \times \dfrac{3}{2} - 4\right) + y\left(4 \times \dfrac{3}{2} - 6\right) - 12 \times \dfrac{3}{2} - 12 = 0$

$\text{Further simplification,}$

$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2x - 12 = 0$

$\text{The required equation when}$~$\lambda = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$x^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}\right) + y^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}\right) + x\left(6 \times \dfrac{2}{3} - 4\right) + y\left(4 \times \dfrac{2}{3} - 6\right) - 12 \times \dfrac{2}{3} - 12 = 0$

$\text{Further simplification,}$

$x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x - 12 = 0$

7285.subject: Mathematics
7285.text: If $\alpha, \beta$ are the two real roots of $4^{\mathrm{tn}}$ roots of unity and $\gamma, \delta$ are the other two roots of it, then the sum of the eccentricities of the conics $|z-\alpha|+|z-\beta|=4$ and $|z-\gamma|+|z-\delta|=6$ is
7285.sol:
The real solutions of $4^{\text{th }}$ root of unity is $\pm$1
$\therefore \alpha=1, \beta=-1$
and other roots are $\pm i\begin{aligned}
& \gamma=i \& \delta=-i \\
& \therefore|z-1|+|z+1|=4 \\
& \Rightarrow|x+i y-1|+|x-i y+1|=4 \\
& \Rightarrow|(x-1)+i y|+|(x+1)-i y|=4 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{(x-1)^2+y^2}=4-\sqrt{(x+1)^2+y^2} \\
& \Rightarrow(x-1)^2+y^2=16+(x+1)^2+y^2-8 \sqrt{(x+1)^2+y^2} \\
& \Rightarrow-4 x=16-8 \sqrt{(x+1)^2+y^2} \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \sqrt{(x+1)^2+y^2}=4+x
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow 4(x+1)^2+4 y^2=(4+x)^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{y^2}{3}=1
\end{aligned}$
which is an ellipse whose eccentricity is
$\Rightarrow e_1=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{1}{2}$
Now, $|z-\gamma|+|z+\delta|=6\Rightarrow|z-i|+|z+i|=6\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow|x+i(y-1)|+|x+i(y+1)|=6 \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{x^2+(y-1)^2}+\sqrt{x^2(y+1)^2}=6

21331.subject: Mathematics
21331.text: The general solution of the differential equation $(x-y) d y=(x+y) d x$ is
21331.sol:
The given differential equation is $(x-y) dy = (x+y) dx$, which can be written as $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x+y}{x-y}$.

This is a homogeneous differential equation. Let $y = vx$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx}$.

Substituting these into the equation, we get $v + x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{x+vx}{x-vx} = \dfrac{1+v}{1-v}$.

$x \dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1+v}{1-v} - v = \dfrac{1+v-v+v^2}{1-v} = \dfrac{1+v^2}{1-v}$.

Separating the variables, we have $\dfrac{1-v}{1+v^2} dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}$.

Integrating both sides, $\int \dfrac{1}{1+v^2} dv - \int \dfrac{v}{1+v^2} dv = \int \dfrac{dx}{x}$.

$\tan^{-1}(v) - \dfrac{1}{2} \ln(1+v^2) = \ln|x| + C_1$.

Substituting $v = \dfrac{y}{x}$, we get $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} \ln\left(1 + \dfrac{y^2}{x^2}\right) = \ln|x| + C_1$.

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \ln|x| + \dfrac{1}{2} \ln\left(\dfrac{x^2+y^2}{x^2}\right) + C_1 = \ln|x| + \dfrac{1}{2} \ln(x^2+y^2) - \ln|x| + C_1$.

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \ln\sqrt{x^2+y^2} + C_1$.

Taking the exponential of both sides, $e^{\tan^{-1}(y/x)} = e^{C_1} \sqrt{x^2+y^2} = c \sqrt{x^2+y^2}$.

Answer: $e^{\tan ^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}=c \sqrt{x^2+y^2}$

21360.subject: Mathematics
21360.text: 164. The solution of the differential equation $\sec ^{2} x \tan y d x+\sec ^{2} y \tan x d y=0$ is
21360.sol:
The given differential equation is $\sec^{2} x \tan y dx + \sec^{2} y \tan x dy = 0$.

Rearranging the terms, we get $\sec^{2} y \tan x dy = -\sec^{2} x \tan y dx$.

Separating the variables, we have $\dfrac{\sec^{2} y}{\tan y} dy = -\dfrac{\sec^{2} x}{\tan x} dx$.

Integrating both sides, $\int \dfrac{\sec^{2} y}{\tan y} dy = -\int \dfrac{\sec^{2} x}{\tan x} dx$.

Let $u = \tan y$, then $du = \sec^{2} y dy$. Let $v = \tan x$, then $dv = \sec^{2} x dx$.

The equation becomes $\int \dfrac{1}{u} du = -\int \dfrac{1}{v} dv$.

Integrating, we get $\ln|u| = -\ln|v| + C_{0}$, which simplifies to $\ln|u| + \ln|v| = C_{0}$.

This implies $\ln|uv| = C_{0}$, or $uv = e^{C_{0}} = C$.

Substituting back $u = \tan y$ and $v = \tan x$, we obtain $\tan y \cdot \tan x = C$.

Answer: $\tan y \cdot \tan x=C$

21540.subject: Mathematics
21540.text: Given that n number of arithmetic means are inserted between two pairs of numbers $a, 2 b$ and $2 a, b$; where $a, b \in \mathbb{R} . If the $m^{$\text{th }$}$ means in the two cases are the same, then the ratio $a: b$ is equal to$
21540.sol:
Let the two numbers be $x$ and $y$. If $n$ arithmetic means $A_1, A_2, ..., A_n$ are inserted between $x$ and $y$, the common difference $d$ is given by $d = \dfrac{y - x}{n + 1}$. The $m^{\text{th}}$ arithmetic mean is $A_m = x + m d = x + m \left( \dfrac{y - x}{n + 1} \right).

For the first pair $a$ and 2b$, the $m^{\text{th}}$ mean is $M_1 = a + m \left( \dfrac{2b - a}{n + 1} \right) = \dfrac{a(n + 1) + m(2b - a)}{n + 1} = \dfrac{an + a + 2bm - am}{n + 1} = \dfrac{a(n - m + 1) + 2bm}{n + 1}.

For the second pair 2a$ and $b$, the $m^{\text{th}}$ mean is $M_2 = 2a + m \left( \dfrac{b - 2a}{n + 1} \right) = \dfrac{2a(n + 1) + m(b - 2a)}{n + 1} = \dfrac{2an + 2a + bm - 2am}{n + 1} = \dfrac{2a(n - m + 1) + bm}{n + 1}.

Given $ M_1 = M_2$, we have $a(n - m + 1) + 2bm = 2a(n - m + 1) + bm$.

Rearranging the terms, 2bm - bm = 2a(n - m + 1) - a(n - m + 1)$, which simplifies to $bm = a(n - m + 1)$.

Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{m}{n - m + 1}$.

Answer: $ m:(n-m+1)$

21772.sol:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 5a & -b \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$.

The property $A \operatorname{adj} A = |A| I$ holds for any square matrix $A$, where $I$ is the identity matrix.

The given equation is $A \operatorname{adj} A = A A^t$. Substituting the property, we have $|A| I = A A^t$.

Calculate the determinant $|A| = (5a)(2) - (-b)(3) = 10a + 3b$.

Calculate $A A^t$:
$A^t = \begin{bmatrix} 5a & 3 \\ -b & 2 \end{bmatrix}$
$A A^t = \begin{bmatrix} 5a & -b \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 5a & 3 \\ -b & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 25a^2 + b^2 & 15a - 2b \\ 15a - 2b & 9 + 4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 25a^2 + b^2 & 15a - 2b \\ 15a - 2b & 13 \end{bmatrix}$.

Equating $|A| I = A A^t$:
$\begin{bmatrix} 10a + 3b & 0 \\ 0 & 10a + 3b \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 25a^2 + b^2 & 15a - 2b \\ 15a - 2b & 13 \end{bmatrix}$.

From the off-diagonal elements, $15a - 2b = 0$, which implies $b = \dfrac{15a}{2}$.

From the bottom-right element, $10a + 3b = 13$.

Substituting $b = \dfrac{15a}{2}$ into the equation $10a + 3b = 13$:
$10a + 3(\dfrac{15a}{2}) = 13$
$10a + \dfrac{45a}{2} = 13$
$\dfrac{20a + 45a}{2} = 13$
$\dfrac{65a}{2} = 13$
$65a = 26 \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{26}{65} = \dfrac{2}{5}$.

Now find $b$:
$b = \dfrac{15}{2} \times \dfrac{2}{5} = 3$.

Calculate $5a + b$:
$5(\dfrac{2}{5}) + 3 = 2 + 3 = 5$.

Answer: 5

21906.subject: Mathematics
21906.text: P and Q are considering to apply for a job. The probability that P applies for the job is $\dfrac{1}{4}$. The probability that $\mathrm{P}$ applies for the job given that $\mathrm{Q}$ applies for the job is $\dfrac{1}{2}$, and the probability that Q applies for the job given that P applies for the job is $\dfrac{1}{3}$. Then the probability that $\mathrm{P}$ does not apply for the job given that $\mathrm{Q}$ does not apply for the job is
21906.sol:
Let $P$ be the event that P applies for the job and $Q$ be the event that Q applies for the job.

Given probabilities are $P(P) = \dfrac{1}{4}$, $P(P|Q) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, and $P(Q|P) = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Using the definition of conditional probability, $P(P \cap Q) = P(Q|P) \times P(P) = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{12}$.

Also, $P(P \cap Q) = P(P|Q) \times P(Q)$, so $\dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times P(Q)$, which gives $P(Q) = \dfrac{2}{12} = \dfrac{1}{6}$.

We need to find $P(P^c | Q^c)$, where $P^c$ and $Q^c$ are the complements of events $P$ and $Q$.

By definition, $P(P^c | Q^c) = \dfrac{P(P^c \cap Q^c)}{P(Q^c)}$.

Using De Morgan's Law, $P(P^c \cap Q^c) = P((P \cup Q)^c) = 1 - P(P \cup Q)$.

The probability $P(P \cup Q) = P(P) + P(Q) - P(P \cap Q) = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{6} - \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{3+2-1}{12} = \dfrac{4}{12} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Thus, $P(P^c \cap Q^c) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

The probability $P(Q^c) = 1 - P(Q) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6}$.

Therefore, $P(P^c | Q^c) = \dfrac{2/3}{5/6} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{6}{5} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{5}$

22007.subject: Mathematics
22007.text: The sum of $n$ terms of the series, $\dfrac{4}{3}+\dfrac{10}{9}+\dfrac{28}{27}+\ldots$ is
22007.sol:
The given series is $\dfrac{4}{3} + \dfrac{10}{9} + \dfrac{28}{27} + \ldots + a_n$.

The $n$-th term $a_n$ can be written as $\dfrac{3^n + 1}{3^n} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{3^n} = 1 + 3^{-n}$.

The sum of $n$ terms is $S_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k = \sum_{k=1}^{n} (1 + 3^{-k}) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^k$.

The first part is $\sum_{k=1}^{n} 1 = n$.

The second part is a geometric progression with first term $a = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and common ratio $r = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

The sum of the geometric series is $\dfrac{a(1 - r^n)}{1 - r} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}(1 - (1/3)^n)}{1 - 1/3} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}(1 - 3^{-n})}{2/3} = \dfrac{1}{2}(1 - 3^{-n}) = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2 \cdot 3^n}$.

Thus, $S_n = n + \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2 \cdot 3^n} = \dfrac{2n + 1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2 \cdot 3^n} = \dfrac{3^n(2n + 1) - 1}{2 \cdot 3^n}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3^n(2 n+1)-1}{2\left(3^n\right)}$

Using $g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$, we get $GM = gR^2$

$v^2 = \dfrac{20gR^2}{11R} = \dfrac{20gR}{11}$

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{20gR}{11}}$

22898.subject: Physics
22898.text: Two spherical planets $P$ and $Q$ have the same uniform density $\rho$, and masses $M_P$ and $M_Q$ and surface areas $A$ and $4 A$ respectively. Another spherical planet R also has the same uniform density $\rho$, and its mass is $\mathrm{Mp}+\mathrm{MQ}$. The escape velocities from these planets is
22898.sol:
The surface area of a sphere is $A = 4 \pi R^2$. Given $A_P = A$ and $A_Q = 4A$, we have $4 \pi R_P^2 = A$ and $4 \pi R_Q^2 = 4A$. This implies $R_Q^2 = 4 R_P^2$, so $R_Q = 2 R_P$.

The mass of a planet with uniform density $\rho$ is $M = \rho \times \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3$. Thus, $M \propto R^3$. Given $R_Q = 2 R_P$, we have $M_Q = (2)^3 M_P = 8 M_P$.

The escape velocity from a planet is $V = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$. Since $M = \rho \times \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3$, we have $V = \sqrt{\dfrac{2G \rho \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3}{R}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8}{3} \pi G \rho} R$. Thus, $V \propto R$.

Since $R_Q = 2 R_P$, it follows that $V_Q = 2 V_P$, so $V_Q > V_P$.

For planet R, $M_R = M_P + M_Q = M_P + 8 M_P = 9 M_P$. Since $M_R = \rho \times \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_R^3$, we have $R_R^3 = \dfrac{M_R}{\rho \dfrac{4}{3} \pi} = \dfrac{9 M_P}{\rho \dfrac{4}{3} \pi} = 9 R_P^3$. Thus, $R_R = 9^{1/3} R_P$.

Since $V \propto R$, $V_R = 9^{1/3} V_P$. Comparing the values: $V_P = 1 V_P$, $V_Q = 2 V_P$, and $V_R = 9^{1/3} V_P \approx 2.08 V_P$.

Therefore, $V_R > V_Q > V_P$.

Answer: $V_R > V_Q > V_P$

25340.text:
Let ${\theta}_{1}, {\theta}_{2}, \ldots , {\theta}_{10}$ be positive valued angles (in radian) such that ${\theta}_{1} + {\theta}_{2} + ⋯ + {\theta}_{10} = 2\pi$. Define the complex numbers ${z}_{1} = {e}^{i{\theta}_{1}}, {z}_{k} = {z}_{k - 1}{e}^{i{\theta}_{k}}$ for $k = 2, 3, \ldots , 10$, where $i = \sqrt{- 1}$. Consider the statements $P$ and $Q$ given below:
$P: \left|{z}_{2} - {z}_{1}\right| + \left|{z}_{3} - {z}_{2}\right| + ⋯ + \left|{z}_{10} - {z}_{9}\right| + \left|{z}_{1} - {z}_{10}\right| \le 2\pi$
$Q: \left|{z}_{2}^{2} - {z}_{1}^{2}\right| + \left|{z}_{3}^{2} - {z}_{2}^{2}\right| + ⋯ + \left|{z}_{10}^{2} - {z}_{9}^{2}\right| + \left|{z}_{1}^{2} - {z}_{10}^{2}\right| \le 4\pi$
25340.sol:
Given,& ${θ}_{1} + {θ}_{2} + . . . . . + {θ}_{10} = 2\pi$,~${z}_{1} = e^{i{θ}_{1}}, {z}_{k} = {z}_{k - 1}e^{i{θ}_{k}}$

Now,~${z}_{k} = {z}_{k - 1}e^{i{θ}_{k}}$

$⇒ {z}_{2} = {z}_{1}e^{i{θ}_{1}}, {z}_{3} = {z}_{2}e^{i{θ}_{2}}, \ldots \ldots$

As,~${z}_{1} = e^{i{θ}_{1}}⇒ \left|{z}_{1}\right| = 1$

${z}_{2} = {z}_{1}e^{i\theta}⇒ \left|{z}_{2}\right| = \left|{z}_{1}\right| = 1$

Similarly~$\left|{z}_{1}\right| = \left|{z}_{2}\right| \ldots = \left|{z}_{k}\right| = 1$

$⇒ {z}_{1}, {z}_{2}, \ldots , {z}_{k}$~lies on a circle of unit radius.

We know,& $\left|{z}_{k} - {z}_{k - 1}\right|$ represents a~line& segment joining ${z}_{k} & {z}_{k - 1}$.

Both~${z}_{k} & {z}_{k - 1}$ lies on a unit circle

Since~${θ}_{1} + {θ}_{2} + . . . . + {θ}_{10} = 2\pi$

We get~

So, $\left|{z}_{2} - {z}_{1}\right|, \left|{z}_{3} - {z}_{2}\right|$, \ldots , $\left|{z}_{1} - {z}_{10}\right|$ are the sides of a decagon circumscribed by a circle~of unit radius

We know, the sum of the length of sides& of a decagon is less than the circumference of its circumcircle.

$⇒ \left|{z}_{2} - {z}_{1}\right| + \left|{z}_{3} - {z}_{2}\right| + ⋯ + \left|{z}_{10} - {z}_{9}\right| + \left|{z}_{1} - {z}_{10}\right| \le 2\pi$

Hence, $P$~is true.

Similarly,& $\left({z}_{1}\right)$2 = e^{i2{θ}_{1}}, $\left({z}_{k}\right)$2 = $\left({z}_{k - 1}\right)$2e^{i2{θ}_{k}}, \ldots \ldots$

So,~\left|{z}_{2}^{2} - {z}_{1}^{2}\right|, \left|{z}_{3}^{2} - {z}_{2}^{2}\right|, \left|{z}_{4}^{2} - {z}_{3}^{2}\right|, \left|{z}_{5}^{2} - {z}_{4}^{2}\right|, \left|{z}_{6}^{2} - {z}_{5}^{2}\right|~are&
the& sides$ of $a pentagon circumscribed by a circle of unit radius

So,& \left|{z}_{2}^{2} - {z}_{1}^{2}\right| + \left|{z}_{3}^{2} - {z}_{2}^{2}\right| + \ldots \left|{z}_{6}^{2} - {z}_{5}^{2}\right| \le 2\pi$

Similarly,~$\left|{z}_{7}^{2} - {z}_{8}^{2}\right|$ + \ldots + $\left|{z}_{1}^{2} - {z}_{10}^{2}\right|$ \le 2\pi$

Adding these~equations, we get

\left|{z}_{2}^{2} - {z}_{1}^{2}\right| + \left|{z}_{3}^{2} - {z}_{2}^{2}\right| + ⋯ + \left|{z}_{10}^{2} - {z}_{9}^{2}\right| + \left|{z}_{1}^{2} - {z}_{10}^{2}\right| \le 4\pi$

Hence,~$Q$& is true.

The Reimer Tiemann reaction is an organic chemical reaction where phenol is converted into an ortho hydroxy benzaldehyde using chloroform, a base, and an acid workup. This reaction can also be described as the chemical reaction used for the ortho-formylation of phenols.

27620.subject: Chemistry
27620.text:
Complete the following reaction sequence and give the name of major product 'P'.
$CH_3-CH_2-C\equiv N \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) } H_3O^+]{\text{(i) } OH^-/H_2O/\Delta} \xrightarrow[\text{(iv) } H_2O]{\text{(iii) } Cl_2/\text{Red P}} P \text{ (Major product)}$
27620.sol:
Step 1: Hydrolysis of the nitrile.
Propanenitrile on basic hydrolysis followed by acidic workup gives propanoic acid:
$CH_3-CH_2-C \equiv N \xrightarrow[(ii)\ H_3O^+]{(i)\ OH^-/H_2O/\Delta} CH_3-CH_2-COOH$

Step 2: Hell$-$Volhard$-$Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction.
Propanoic acid has an $sp^3$ $\alpha$-carbon bearing two $\alpha$-hydrogens. In the HVZ reaction, $Cl_2$ in the presence of red phosphorus selectively replaces one $\alpha$-hydrogen by chlorine, giving the $\alpha$-chloro acid after aqueous workup:
$CH_3-CH_2-COOH \xrightarrow[(iv)\ H_2O]{(iii)\ Cl_2/\text{Red P}} CH_3-CH(Cl)-COOH$

Hence, the major product $P$ is $2$-chloropropanoic acid, which corresponds to option $(1)$.

28364.subject: Chemistry
28364.text: The reaction used for preparation of soap from fat is :
28364.sol: The reaction used for preparation of soap from fat is not alkaline hydrolysis, but rather saponification. In saponification, a triglyceride (fat or oil) is reacted with a strong base, such as sodium hydroxide (or potassium hydroxide, in the presence of heat to produce soap molecules and glycerol as a byproduct. The reaction involves the hydrolysis of the ester bond in the triglyceride by the base to form carboxylate ions (the soap molecules) and glycerol.

28395.text:
Match List - I with List - II.

List-I List-II
A I Dishwashing powder
B II Toothpaste
C ${C}_{17}{H}_{35}{COO}^{-}{Na}^{+} + {Na}_{2}{CO}_{3} +$ Rosinate III Laundry soap
D ${CH}_{3}{\left({CH}_{2}\right)}_{16}COO{\left({CH}_{2}{CH}_{2}O\right)}_{n}{CH}_{2}{CH}_{2}OH$ IV Hair conditioner

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
28395.sol:
1. Laundry soaps contain fillers like sodium rosinate, sodium silicate, borax and sodium carbonate.

2. Cationic detergents are quaternary ammonium salts of amines with acetates, chlorides or bromides as anions. Cationic part possess a long hydrocarbon chain and a positive charge on nitrogen atom. Hence, these are called cationic detergents. Cetyltrimethylammonium bromide is a popular cationic detergent and is used in hair conditioners.

3. Non-ionic Detergents: Non-ionic detergents do not contain any ion in their constitution. One such detergent is formed when stearic acid reacts with polyethyleneglycol. Liquid dishwashing detergents are non-ionic type.

4. In anionic detergents, the anionic part of the molecule is involved in the cleansing action. Sodium salts of alkylbenzenesulphonates are an important class of anionic detergents. They are mostly used for household work.

30639.subject: Chemistry
30639.text: Which hydride among the following is less stable?
30639.sol: ${BeH}_{2}$ is indeed considered to be less stable compared to other hydrides among the given due to its significant covalent character and electron deficiency. Beryllium, being a small and highly charged cation, attracts the electrons in the $Be - H$ bonds more strongly, resulting in a greater degree of electron sharing between beryllium and hydrogen. This covalent character is in contrast to other alkaline earth metal hydrides, which tend to have more ionic character.

30983.subject: Chemistry
30983.text:
Regarding the hydrides of group 15 elements $\mathrm{EH}_{3}(\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{N}, \mathrm{P}, \mathrm{As}, \mathrm{Sb})$, select the correct statement from the following:
A. The stability of hydrides decreases down the group.
B. The basicity of hydrides decreases down the group.
C. The reducing character increases down the group.
D. The boiling point increases down the group.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
30983.sol:
For group 15 hydrides $EH_3$ (N, P, As, Sb):
Statement A is correct—stability decreases down the group as H-E bond strength decreases.
Statement B is correct—basicity decreases as the central atom becomes less electronegative, making it less willing to share electron pairs.
Statement C is correct—reducing character increases down the group as the hydrides become easier to oxidize.
Statement D is incorrect—boiling points do not consistently increase; NH₃ is anomalously high (-33°C) due to strong hydrogen bonding, but PH₃ (-87°C) is lower, and the trend is irregular.

Therefore, A, B & C only are correct.

31651.subject: Chemistry
31651.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The Henry's law constant $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}$ is constant with respect to variations in solution's concentration over the range for which the solution is ideally dilute.
Statement II: $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}$ does not differ for the same solute in different solvents.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
31651.sol:
Statement I: $K_H$ is constant with respect to concentration variations in ideally dilute solutions.
TRUE - Henry's law constant depends only on temperature and the nature of the solute-solvent interaction. For ideally dilute solutions, $K_H$ = $P_\text{gas}/x_\text{solute}$ remains constant regardless of solute concentration within the dilute range.

Statement II: $K_H$ does not differ for the same solute in different solvents.
FALSE - Henry's law constant is solvent-dependent. The same gas or solute has different $K_H$ values in different solvents at the same temperature because the solute-solvent interactions differ. For example, CO₂ dissolves differently in water versus ethanol, giving different $K_H$ values.

Therefore, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

32597.text:
Two reactions are given below:
$2{Fe}_{( s )} + \dfrac{3}{2}{O}_{2 ( g )} \to {Fe}_{2}{O}_{3 ( s )}, \Delta{H}^{o} = - 822kJ / mol$

${C}_{( s )} + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2 ( g )} \to {CO}_{( g )}, \Delta{H}^{o} = - 110kJ / mol$

$3{C}_{( s )} + {Fe}_{2}{O}_{3 ( s )} \to 2{Fe}_{( s )} + 3{CO}_{( g )}$
32597.sol:
Enthalpy change is the standard enthalpy of formation, in any general chemical reaction, the reactants undergo chemical changes and combine to give products. It can be represented by the following equation:

$Reactant \to Product$

From the given equations,

$2{Fe}_{( s )} + \dfrac{3}{2}{O}_{2 ( g )} \to {Fe}_{2}{O}_{3 ( s )}, \Delta{H}^{o} = - 822kJ / mol$ .........(i)

${C}_{( s )} + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2 ( g )} \to {CO}_{( g )}, \Delta H ° = - 110kJ / mol$....(ii)

$3{C}_{( s )} + {Fe}_{2}{O}_{3 ( s )} \to 2{Fe}_{( s )} + 3{CO}_{( g )}, {\Delta H}_{3} = ?$

The value of ${\Delta H}_{3}$ can be calculated as,

${\Delta H}_{3} = 3 \times {\Delta H}_{2} - {\Delta H}_{1}$

$= 3 ( - 110 ) + 822$

$= 492kJ / mole$

33276.subject: Mathematics
33276.text: The coefficient of $x^2$ in the expansion of $\left(2x^2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{10}$, $x \neq 0$, is :
33276.sol:
The general term in the expansion of $\left(2x^2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{10}$ is given by:

$T_{r+1} = ^{10}C_{r} (2x^2)^{10-r} \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^r$

$T_{r+1} = ^{10}C_{r} 2^{10-r} x^{20-2r} x^{-r}$

$T_{r+1} = ^{10}C_{r} 2^{10-r} x^{20-3r}$

For the coefficient of $x^2$, we equate the power of $x$ to $2$:

$20 - 3r = 2$

$3r = 18 \Rightarrow r = 6$

Substituting $r = 6$ in the coefficient part, we get:

Coefficient $= ^{10}C_{6} 2^{10-6}$

$= ^{10}C_{4} 2^4$

$= \dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} \times 16$

$= 210 \times 16$

$= 3360$

Answer: $3360$

33360.text: If $C3 2n : C3 n = 10: 1,$ then the ratio $\left({n}^{2} + 3n\right): \left({n}^{2} - 3n + 4\right) is$
33360.sol:
We have been given that $C3 2n : C3 n = 10$

We know that $Cr n = \dfrac{n !}{r ! \left(n - r\right) !}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{\left(2n\right) !}{3 ! \left(2n - 3\right) !}}{\dfrac{n !}{3 ! \left(n - 3\right) !}} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(2n\right) !}{3 ! \left(2n - 3\right) !} \times \dfrac{3 ! \left(n - 3\right) !}{n !} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(2n\right)\left(2n - 1\right)\left(2n - 2\right)\left(2n - 3\right) !}{\left(2n - 3\right) !} \times \dfrac{\left(n - 3\right) !}{n\left(n - 1\right)\left(n - 2\right)\left(n - 3\right) !} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(2n\right)\left(2n - 1\right)\left(2n - 2\right)}{n\left(n - 1\right)\left(n - 2\right)} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(4\right)\left(2n - 1\right)}{\left(n - 2\right)} = 10$

$⇒ 8n - 4 = 10n - 20$

$⇒ n = 8$

Hence, the value of $\dfrac{{n}^{2} + 3n}{{n}^{2} - 3n + 4}$ is $= \dfrac{{8}^{2} + 3\left(8\right)}{{8}^{2} - 3\left(8\right) + 4} = \dfrac{88}{44} = 2$

Therefore, the value of $\dfrac{{n}^{2} + 3n}{{n}^{2} - 3n + 4}$ is $2: 1$.

34945.text: If ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + siny = 4$, then the value of $\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}}$ at the point $\left(- 2, 0\right)$ is :
34945.sol:
Given ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + siny = 4$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get

$2x + \left(2y + cosy\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- 2x}{2y + cos ⁡ y}$

At $\left(- 2, 0\right), \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{4}{1} = 4$

Also, $\left(2y + cosy\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2x = 0$

35059.text: Let the length of the latus rectum of an ellipse with its major axis along $x$ -axis and centre at the origin, be 8 . If the distance between the foci of this ellipse is equal to the length of its minor axis, then which one of the following points lies on it?
35059.sol:
Let the ellipse be $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$

Then, $\frac{2 b^{2}}{a}=8,2 a e-b^{2}$ and $b^{2}=a^{3}\left(1-e^{2}\right)$

$\Rightarrow a=8, b^{2}=32$

Then, the equation of the ellipse

$\frac{x^{2}}{64}+\frac{y^{2}}{32}=1$

Hence, the point $(4 \sqrt{3}, 2 \sqrt{2})$ lies on the ellipse.

35100.subject: Mathematics
35100.text: Let for some $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, $f:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be a function satisfying $f(x+y)=f(x)+2y^2+y+\alpha xy$ for all $x,y \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f(0)=-1$ and $f(1)=2$, then the value of $\sum_{n=1}^{5}(\alpha+f(n))$ is:
35100.sol:
Given $f(x+y) = f(x) + 2y^2 + y + \alpha xy$

Substituting $x = 0$ and replacing $y$ with $x$, we get:

$f(x) = f(0) + 2x^2 + x + \alpha(0)x$

Since $f(0) = -1$, we have:

$f(x) = 2x^2 + x - 1$

To find $\alpha$, substitute $f(x)$ into the original functional equation:

$2(x+y)^2 + (x+y) - 1 = (2x^2 + x - 1) + 2y^2 + y + \alpha xy$

$2x^2 + 4xy + 2y^2 + x + y - 1 = 2x^2 + x - 1 + 2y^2 + y + \alpha xy$

Comparing both sides, we get $\alpha = 4$.

We need to find the value of $\sum_{n=1}^{5}(\alpha+f(n))$:

$\sum_{n=1}^{5}(4 + 2n^2 + n - 1) = \sum_{n=1}^{5}(2n^2 + n + 3)$

$= 2\sum_{n=1}^{5}n^2 + \sum_{n=1}^{5}n + \sum_{n=1}^{5}3$

$= 2\left(\dfrac{5 \times 6 \times 11}{6}\right) + \dfrac{5 \times 6}{2} + 3 \times 5$

$= 2(55) + 15 + 15$

$= 110 + 30 = 140$

Answer: $140$

37555.text: Let the mean and the variance of $20$ observations ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, \ldots {x}_{20}$ be $15$ and $9$, respectively. For $\alpha \in R$, if the mean of ${\left({x}_{1} + \alpha\right)}^{2}, {\left({x}_{2} + \alpha\right)}^{2}, \ldots , {\left({x}_{20} + \alpha\right)}^{2}$ is $178$, then the square of the maximum value of $\alpha$ is equal to ______.
37555.sol:
Given,

Mean of observation is $15$,

So $\dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}}{20} = 15$

$⇒ ∑ {x}_{i} = 15 \times 20 = 300 ⋯ \left(i\right)$

Also variance is given as $9$

So, $\dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}^{2}}{20} - {\left(\dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}}{20}\right)}^{2} = 9 ⋯ \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}^{2}}{20} - {\left(15\right)}^{2} = 9 ⋯ \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ ∑ {x}_{i}^{2} = 234 \times 20 = 4680$

Given mean of ${\left({x}_{1} + \alpha\right)}^{2}, {\left({x}_{2} + \alpha\right)}^{2}, \ldots , {\left({x}_{20} + \alpha\right)}^{2}$ is $178$

So, $\dfrac{∑ {\left({x}_{i} + \alpha\right)}^{2}}{20} = 178 ⇒ ∑ {\left({x}_{i} + \alpha\right)}^{2} = 3560$

$⇒ ∑ {x}_{i}^{2} + 2\alpha ∑ {x}_{i} + ∑ {\alpha}^{2} = 3560$

$⇒ 4680 + 600\alpha + 20{\alpha}^{2} = 3560$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} + 30\alpha + 56 = 0$

$⇒ \left(\alpha + 28\right)\left(\alpha + 2\right) = 0$

$\alpha = - 2, - 28$

Square of maximum value of $\alpha$ is $4$

37998.text: Let the plane $P: 4x - y + z = 10$ be rotated by an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ about its line of intersection with the plane $x + y - z = 4$. If $\alpha$ is the distance of the point $( 2, 3, - 4 )$ from the new position of the plane $P$, then $35\alpha$ is equal to
37998.sol:
We know that if a plane passes through the line of intersection of planes ${P}_{1} and {P}_{2}$ then the family of planes is given by ${P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2}$ where $\lambda \in R$.

Equation of plane after rotation :

$\left(4x - y + z - 10\right) + \lambda\left(x + y - z - 4\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 + \lambda\right)x + y\left(\lambda - 1\right) + z\left(1 - \lambda\right) - 4\lambda - 10 = 0$

Now angle between the new plane and $4x - y + z - 10$ is $90 °$.

$⇒ \overset{\to}{n}1 \cdot \overset{\to}{n}2 = 0$

$⇒ \left(4 + \lambda\right)4 + \left(\lambda - 1\right)\left(- 1\right) + \left(1 - \lambda\right)1 = 0$

$⇒ 16 + 4\lambda - \lambda + 1 + 1 - \lambda = 0$

$⇒ 2\lambda = - 18$

$⇒ \lambda = - 9$

$∴$ Equation of plane : $– 5x – 10y + 10z + 26 = 0$

Distance of plane from $( 2, 3, – 4 )$

$= \left|\dfrac{- 10 - 30 - 40 + 26}{\sqrt{25 + 100 + 100}}\right| = \dfrac{54}{15} = \alpha$

$35\alpha = 35 \cdot \dfrac{54}{15} = 7 \times \dfrac{54}{3} = 7 \times 18 = 126$

Hence this is the required option.

38021.sol:
Given,

The equation of the plane passing through the line of intersection of the planes $2x - y + z = 3, 4x - 3y + 5z + 9 = 0$ and parallel to the line $\dfrac{x + 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{y + 3}{4} = \dfrac{z - 2}{5}$ is $ax + by + cz + 6 = 0,$

Now let, ${P}_{1} = 2x - y + z = 3$

And ${P}_{2} = 4x - 3y + 5z + 9 = 0$

Now using family of planes we get,

${P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2} = 0$

$⇒ ( 2x - y + z - 3 ) + \lambda ( 4x - 3y + 5z + 9 ) = 0$

$⇒ ( 2 + 4\lambda ) x - ( 1 + 3\lambda ) y + ( 1 + 5\lambda ) z - ( 3 - 9\lambda ) = 0$

Now let,

${P}_{3} = ( 2 + 4\lambda ) x - ( 1 + 3\lambda ) y + ( 1 + 5\lambda ) z - ( 3 - 9\lambda ) = 0$

Now given ${P}_{3}$ is parallel to line,

$\dfrac{x + 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{y + 3}{4} = \dfrac{z - 2}{5}$

So, using perpendicular condition as normal vector of plane will be perpendicular to given line we get,

$- 2 ( 2 + 4\lambda ) - 4 ( 1 + 3\lambda ) + 5 ( 1 + 5\lambda ) = 0$

$⇒ - 3 + 5\lambda = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{3}{5}$

Hence, equation of plane ${P}_{3}$ will be,

${P}_{3}: \dfrac{22x}{5} - \dfrac{14y}{5} + \dfrac{20z}{5} + \dfrac{12}{5} = 0$

$⇒ {P}_{3} = 11x - 7y + 10z + 6 = 0$

Now on comparing with $ax + by + cz + 6 = 0,$ we get,

$a = 11$, $b = - 7$ and $c = 10$

$∴ a + b + c = 11 - 7 + 10 = 14$

41031.text:
A mixture of carbon dioxide and oxygen has volume $8310$ cm$^3$, temperature $300$ K, pressure $100$ kPa and mass $13.2$ g. The number of moles of carbon dioxide and oxygen gases in the mixture respectively are _______.
(Assume both carbon dioxide and oxygen gases behave like ideal gases) $[R = 8.31$ J/mol.K$]$
41031.sol:
Using the ideal gas equation, the total number of moles of the mixture is given by:

$n = \dfrac{PV}{RT}$

Substituting the given values:
$P = 100 \text{ kPa} = 10^5 \text{ Pa}$
$V = 8310 \text{ cm}^3 = 8.31 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^3$
$T = 300 \text{ K}$
$R = 8.31 \text{ J/(mol}\cdot\text{K)}$

$n = \dfrac{10^5 \times 8.31 \times 10^{-3}}{8.31 \times 300} = \dfrac{100}{300} = \dfrac{1}{3} \text{ mol}$

Let $n_1$ and $n_2$ be the number of moles of $CO_2$ and $O_2$ respectively.

$n_1 + n_2 = \dfrac{1}{3}$

The total mass of the mixture is $13.2 \text{ g}$. Using the molar masses of $CO_2$ ($44 \text{ g/mol}$) and $O_2$ ($32 \text{ g/mol}$):

$44n_1 + 32n_2 = 13.2$

Substituting $n_2 = \dfrac{1}{3} - n_1$ into the mass equation:

$44n_1 + 32\left(\dfrac{1}{3} - n_1\right) = 13.2$

$12n_1 + \dfrac{32}{3} = 13.2$

$12n_1 = \dfrac{39.6 - 32}{3} = \dfrac{7.6}{3}$

$n_1 = \dfrac{7.6}{36} = \dfrac{19}{90} \approx 0.21 \text{ mol}$

The number of moles of $O_2$ is:

$n_2 = \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{19}{90} = \dfrac{11}{90} \approx 0.12 \text{ mol}$

The number of moles of $CO_2$ and $O_2$ are $0.21$ and $0.12$ respectively.

Answer: $0.21$ and $0.12$

42958.text: In a reflecting telescope, a secondary mirror is used to:
options: reduce the problem of mechanical support
move the eyepiece outside the telescopic tube
42958.sol:
Mirrors are used in reflecting telescopes, which allow astronomers to see distant objects in space more clearly.

A mirror forms an image by gathering light from spatial objects. A second mirror receives the picture that was reflected by the first mirror, which may be rather wide. The light is reflected by this tiny mirror onto an eyepiece lens, which magnifies or enlarges the image of the object.

Hence, the secondary mirror is used to move the eyepiece outside the telescopic tube.

44098.text: If force $( F )$, velocity $( V )$ and time $( T )$ are considered as fundamental physical quantity, then dimensional formula of density will be :
44098.sol:
The dimensional formula of force is

$F = ML{T}^{- 2}$

The dimensional formula of velocity is

$V = L{T}^{- 1}$

The formula for density is

Density $= \dfrac{M}{{L}^{3}} = M{L}^{- 3}$

Comparing the density dimensions with the assumed fundamental quantities in the question,
$M{L}^{- 3} = {\left[F\right]}^{x}{\left[V\right]}^{y}{\left[T\right]}^{z} ⇒ M{L}^{- 3} = {\left[ML{T}^{- 2}\right]}^{x}{\left[L{T}^{- 1}\right]}^{y} [ T{]}^{z} ⇒ M{L}^{- 3} = {M}^{x}{L}^{( x + y )}{T}^{- 2x - y + z}$

Comparing the exponents,
$x = 1 . . . ( i ) x + y = - 3 . . . ( ii ) - 2x - y + z = 0 . . . ( iii )$

Solving equations (i), (ii) & (iii), we get

$y = - 4, z = - 2$.

The dimensions of density $= F{V}^{- 4}{T}^{- 2}$.

46522.text: Two simple pendulums of length 0.5 m and 20 m respectively are given small linear displacement in one direction at the same time. They will again be in the phase when the pendulum of shorter length has completed $x$ oscillations, where $x$ is
46522.sol:
Time period of simple pendulum
For Ist pendulum $\begin{aligned} T_1 & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{5}{g}} \\ & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{5}{9.8}}=\sqrt{20} \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$
For IInd pendulum $T_2=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{20}{g}}$
$=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{20}{9.8}}=2 \sqrt{20} \mathrm{~s}$
Suppose the time will be in same phase is $t$ then
$\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{t} & =\frac{1}{T_1}-\frac{1}{T_2} \\ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{20}}-\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{20}}\end{aligned}$
$=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{20}}$
So, $\quad t=2 \sqrt{20}$
Hence, the number of oscillation of simple pendulum of shorter length $(x)=\frac{2 \sqrt{20}}{\sqrt{20}}=2$.

As Universe expanded, the temperature came down.
Hydrogen and Helium gases formed before the explosion.

47297.subject: Biology
47297.text: In a practical examination, the below given pedigree chart was given as spotter for identification. The students identified the pedigree chart as ____
47297.sol:
If the trait were sex-linked recessive, the affected mother in generation I would have only affected sons. Since she has an unaffected son in generation II, it is not sex-linked recessive.

The trait appears in all generations, indicating a dominant trait. Assuming it is autosomal dominant, let the affected allele be A$ and the normal allele be $a$.

The affected female in generation I must be heterozygous (Aa$) because she has unaffected offspring (aa$). Her unaffected partner is $aa$.

The cross $Aa \times aa$ produces both affected (Aa$) and unaffected (aa$) offspring, which matches the observed progeny in generation II.

Similarly, the affected female in generation II (Aa$) and her unaffected partner (aa$) produce both affected (Aa$) and unaffected (aa$) offspring in generation III, consistent with the pedigree.

This is a classic textbook pedigree for an autosomal dominant trait like myotonic dystrophy.

Answer: Autosomal dominant$

54893.subject: Chemistry
54893.text: Identify the final product obtained when a mixture of vapours of phenol and hydrogen is passed over nickel catalyst at 433 K.
54893.sol:
Catalytic hydrogenation of phenol under nickel catalyst at $433\, \text{K}$ results in saturation of the aromatic ring while preserving the hydroxyl group.

The benzene ring undergoes complete hydrogenation, requiring $3$ equivalents of $\text{H}_2$: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 3\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni, 433 K}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{OH}$.

This yields cyclohexanol, where the aromatic system is reduced to a saturated cyclohexane ring with the $-\text{OH}$ group retained. Partial reduction or deoxygenation does not occur under these conditions.

Final answer: $\boxed{A}$

54909.subject: Chemistry
54909.text: Which among the following compounds has lowest boiling point?
54909.sol:
Boiling point in isomeric alcohols depends primarily on molecular branching. Increased branching reduces surface area, weakening van der Waals forces between molecules.

For $\mathrm{C_4 H_{10} O}$ isomers:
Bu\tan^{-1}-ol ($\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2 CH_2 CH_2 OH}$) is straight-chain
Butan-2-ol ($\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2 CH(OH)CH_3 }$) has minimal branching
2-Methylpropan-1-ol ($\mathrm{(CH_3 )_2 CHCH_2 OH}$) shows moderate branching
2-Methylpropan-2-ol ($\mathrm{(CH_3 )_3 COH}$) is maximally branched

The compact, spherical shape of 2-methylpropan-2-ol minimizes intermolecular contact area, resulting in the weakest van der Waals interactions. Experimental boiling points confirm this ordering: approximately $117^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $100^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $108^\circ\mathrm{C}$, and $83^\circ\mathrm{C}$ respectively.

55432.subject: Chemistry
55432.text: Which of the following has largest size?
55432.sol:
The size of the given biological entities generally follows the order: Antibody < Virus < Bacteria < Cancer cell.

Antibodies are protein molecules and are the smallest (around $10$ to $15$ nm).

Viruses are infectious agents composed of genetic material and protein coats, typically ranging from $20$ to $300$ nm.

Bacteria are prokaryotic cells, usually measuring between $1$ to $10\mu$ m.

Cancer cells are eukaryotic animal cells, which are the largest among the given options, typically ranging from $10$ to $30\mu$ m or more.

Therefore, a cancer cell has the largest size.

Answer: Cancer cell

55751.subject: Chemistry
55751.text: Which is the correct decreasing order of boiling points for different compounds from following ?
55751.sol:
The boiling point of haloalkanes increases with an increase in the molecular mass and the size of the halogen atom due to the stronger van der Waals forces of attraction.

Comparing the given compounds:
$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ has one chlorine atom.
$\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$ has one bromine atom, which is heavier and larger than chlorine.
$\text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2$ has two bromine atoms.
$\text{CHBr}_3$ has three bromine atoms.

The molecular mass follows the order: $\text{CHBr}_3 > \text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2 > \text{CH}_3\text{Br} > \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$.

Therefore, the decreasing order of boiling points is $\text{CHBr}_3 > \text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2 > \text{CH}_3\text{Br} > \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$.

Answer: $\text{CHBr}_3 > \text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2 > \text{CH}_3\text{Br} > \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$

55770.subject: Chemistry
55770.text: In the compound ${}^1\text{CH}_2 = {}^2\text{CH} - {}^3\text{CH}_2 - {}^4\text{CH}_2 - {}^5\text{C} \equiv {}^6\text{CH}$, The $C_2 - C_3$ bond is of type
55770.sol:
The given compound is $^{1}\text{CH}_2 = ^{2}\text{CH} - ^{3}\text{CH}_2 - ^{4}\text{CH}_2 - ^{5}\text{C} \equiv ^{6}\text{CH}$.

The hybridization of a carbon atom is determined by the number of sigma bonds it forms.

Carbon atom $C_2$ is bonded to one carbon atom via a double bond, one carbon atom via a single bond, and one hydrogen atom via a single bond. It forms $3$ sigma bonds and $1$ pi bond. Thus, $C_2$ is $sp^2$ hybridized.

Carbon atom $C_3$ is bonded to two carbon atoms via single bonds and two hydrogen atoms via single bonds. It forms $4$ sigma bonds and $0$ pi bonds. Thus, $C_3$ is $sp^3$ hybridized.

Therefore, the $C_2 - C_3$ bond is formed by the overlap of $sp^2$ and $sp^3$ hybridized orbitals, making it an $sp^2 - sp^3$ type bond.

Answer: $sp^2 - sp^3$

56673.text: What is the number of unpaired electrons in Ti in + 3 state?
56673.sol:
Titanium has atomic number 22 with ground state configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^2 4s^2$. The $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ ion results from removal of three electrons, taken first from the $4s$ orbital followed by the $3d$ orbital, yielding configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3d^1$.

In the $3d^1$ configuration, the single electron occupies one of the five d orbitals with unpaired spin. Applying Hund's rule confirms this electron remains unpaired.

The number of unpaired electrons in $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ is $\boxed{1}$.

57956.subject: Chemistry
57956.text: Calculate the molar concentration of weak monobasic acid if $K_a = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}$ and degree of dissociation is $0.01$ ?
57956.sol:
For a weak monobasic acid, the dissociation constant is given by:

$K_a = \dfrac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}$

Since $\alpha = 0.01$, which is very small compared to $1$, we can approximate $1-\alpha \approx 1$.

$K_a = C\alpha^2$

Rearranging for $C$:

$C = \dfrac{K_a}{\alpha^2}$

Substituting the given values:

$C = \dfrac{1.8 \times 10^{-5}}{(0.01)^2}$

$C = \dfrac{1.8 \times 10^{-5}}{10^{-4}}$

$C = 1.8 \times 10^{-1}$ M

Answer: $1.8 \times 10^{-1}$

60245.subject: Mathematics
60245.text: If $\mathrm{y}=\alpha \log x+\beta x^3-x$ has extreme values at $x=-1$ and $x=1$, then $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are respectively
60245.sol:
Finding Extreme Values via Derivatives

The function $y = \alpha \log x + \beta x^3 - x$ has extreme values where its first derivative $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$. Differentiate term by term:

$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\alpha}{x} + 3\beta x^2 - 1$

Given extreme points at $x = 1$ and $x = -1$, evaluate $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at both points:

At $x = 1$: $\frac{\alpha}{1} + 3\beta (1)^2 - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha + 3\beta = 1$

At $x = -1$: $\frac{\alpha}{-1} + 3\beta (-1)^2 - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow -\alpha + 3\beta = 1$

Add the two equations to eliminate $\alpha$:

$(\alpha + 3\beta) + (-\alpha + 3\beta) = 1 + 1 \Rightarrow 6\beta = 2 \Rightarrow \beta = \frac{1}{3}$

Substitute $\beta = \frac{1}{3}$ into $\alpha + 3\beta = 1$:

$\alpha + 3 \cdot \frac{1}{3} = 1 \Rightarrow \alpha + 1 = 1 \Rightarrow \alpha = 0$

The solution $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = \frac{1}{3}$ corresponds to option A.

Final Answer: $\boxed{A}$

60569.text: If the area bounded by the curve $x^2 = by$ and the lines $y = 1, y = 4$ in the first quadrant is $28$ sq. units, then the value of b is...
60569.sol:
The equation of the curve is $x^2 = by$. In the first quadrant, $x = \sqrt{b}\sqrt{y}$.

The area bounded by the curve and the lines $y = 1$ and $y = 4$ in the first quadrant is given by:

$\int_{1}^{4} x \, dy = 28$

$\int_{1}^{4} \sqrt{b}\sqrt{y} \, dy = 28$

$\sqrt{b} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} y^{3/2} \right]_{1}^{4} = 28$

$\dfrac{2}{3} \sqrt{b} (4^{3/2} - 1^{3/2}) = 28$

$\dfrac{2}{3} \sqrt{b} (8 - 1) = 28$

$\dfrac{14}{3} \sqrt{b} = 28$

$\sqrt{b} = 28 \times \dfrac{3}{14}$

$\sqrt{b} = 6$

$b = 36$

Answer: $36$

60682.subject: Mathematics
60682.text: If $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$, then which of the following statements is not true?
60682.sol:
Given the set $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$.

Checking the first statement: $\exists x \in A$, such that $x + 4 \leq 9$. For $x = 1$, $1 + 4 = 5 \leq 9$. This statement is true.

Checking the second statement: $\exists x \in A$, such that $12 - x = 7$. Solving for $x$ gives $x = 5$. Since $5 \in A$, this statement is true.

Checking the third statement: $\forall x \in A, x + 3 \geq 4$. The minimum value of $x$ in $A$ is $1$. For $x = 1$, $1 + 3 = 4 \geq 4$. For all other values in $A$, $x + 3 > 4$. This statement is true.

Checking the fourth statement: $\exists x \in A$, such that $x + 2 < 3$. Solving for $x$ gives $x < 1$. There is no element in $A$ that is strictly less than $1$. This statement is false.

Therefore, the fourth statement is not true.

Answer: $\exists x \in A$, such that $x + 2 < 3$

These are parabolas with vertices at the origin and axes along the Y-axis.

A: Family of circles (incorrect)

B: Family of parabolas with vertex at origin along positive Y-axis (correct)

C: Family with axis along X-axis (incorrect)

63593.text:
A random variable X has the following probability distribution
$X = x$$1$$2$$3$$4$$5$$6$$7$$8$
$P(X=x)$$0.15$$0.23$$0.10$$0.12$$0.20$$0.08$$0.07$$0.05$

For the events $E = \{X \text{ is a prime number}\}$, $F = \{X < 4\}$, $P(E \cup F)$ is
63593.sol:
The event $E$ is that $X$ is a prime number. From the given values of $X$, the prime numbers are $2, 3, 5, 7$.

$E = \{2, 3, 5, 7\}$

The event $F$ is that $X < 4$. From the given values of $X$, the numbers less than $4$ are $1, 2, 3$.

$F = \{1, 2, 3\}$

The union of events $E$ and $F$ is:

$E \cup F = \{1, 2, 3, 5, 7\}$

The probability $P(E \cup F)$ is the sum of the probabilities of these individual outcomes:

$P(E \cup F) = P(X=1) + P(X=2) + P(X=3) + P(X=5) + P(X=7)$

Substituting the given probabilities:

$P(E \cup F) = 0.15 + 0.23 + 0.10 + 0.20 + 0.07 = 0.75$

Answer: $0.75$

65106.subject: Mathematics
65106.text: Let ABCD be a quadrilateral with $\overline{AB} = \vec{a}$, $\overline{AD} = \vec{b}$ and $\overline{AC} = 3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}$. If its area is $\alpha$ times the area of the parallelogram with AB, AD as adjacent sides, then the value of $\alpha$ is equal to
65106.sol:
The area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is given by:

$\Delta_1 = |\overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AD}| = |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$

The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ can be calculated using its diagonals $\overrightarrow{AC}$ and $\overrightarrow{BD}$:

$\Delta_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} |\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{BD}|$

The diagonal vector $\overrightarrow{BD}$ is:

$\overrightarrow{BD} = \overrightarrow{AD} - \overrightarrow{AB} = \vec{b} - \vec{a}$

Taking the cross product of the diagonals:

$\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{BD} = (3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}) \times (\vec{b} - \vec{a})$

$\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{BD} = 3(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) - 3(\vec{a} \times \vec{a}) + 2(\vec{b} \times \vec{b}) - 2(\vec{b} \times \vec{a})$

Since $\vec{a} \times \vec{a} = \vec{0}$, $\vec{b} \times \vec{b} = \vec{0}$, and $\vec{b} \times \vec{a} = -(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$:

$\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{BD} = 3(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) - \vec{0} + \vec{0} + 2(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) = 5(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

Substituting this back into the area formula for the quadrilateral:

$\Delta_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} |5(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})| = \dfrac{5}{2} |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$

Given that $\Delta_2 = \alpha \Delta_1$:

$\dfrac{5}{2} |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}| = \alpha |\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|$

$\alpha = \dfrac{5}{2}$

66295.text: In meter bridge experiment, two resistances X and Y in the two gaps give a null point dividing the wire in the ratio $2 : 3$. When each resistance is increased by $30\,\Omega$, the null point divides the wire in the ratio $5 : 6$. The resistance X and Y are respectively
66295.sol:
For a meter bridge, the ratio of resistances in the two gaps is equal to the ratio of the balancing lengths.

Initially, the null point divides the wire in the ratio $2 : 3$.

$\dfrac{X}{Y} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\Rightarrow Y = \dfrac{3}{2}X$

When each resistance is increased by $30\,\Omega$, the new ratio becomes $5 : 6$.

$\dfrac{X + 30}{Y + 30} = \dfrac{5}{6}$

$\Rightarrow 6X + 180 = 5Y + 150$

Substituting $Y = \dfrac{3}{2}X$ into the equation:

$6X + 180 = 5\left(\dfrac{3}{2}X\right) + 150$

$6X - \dfrac{15}{2}X = 150 - 180$

$-\dfrac{3}{2}X = -30$

$X = 20\,\Omega$

Substituting the value of $X$ to find $Y$:

$Y = \dfrac{3}{2}(20) = 30\,\Omega$

Answer: $20\,\Omega$ , $30\,\Omega$

66770.text: Two solenoids A and B of equal number of turns have their lengths and radii in the same ratio $1 : 3$. The ratio of the self-inductance of solenoid A to that of B will be
66770.sol:
The self-inductance of a solenoid is given by the formula $L = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l} = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 \pi r^2}{l}$

Given that the number of turns are equal, $N_A = N_B$.

The ratio of their lengths is $\dfrac{l_A}{l_B} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

The ratio of their radii is $\dfrac{r_A}{r_B} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Taking the ratio of their self-inductances:

$\dfrac{L_A}{L_B} = \left(\dfrac{r_A}{r_B}\right)^2 \times \dfrac{l_B}{l_A}$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{L_A}{L_B} = \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 \times\left(\dfrac{3}{1}\right)

\dfrac{L_A}{L_B} = \dfrac{1}{9} \times3 = \dfrac{1}{3}

The ratio of the self-inductance of solenoid A to that of B is 1 : 3$.

Answer: $1 : 3$

68025.text: The error in the measurement of length and mass is $3 \%$ and $4 \%$ respectively. The error in the measurement of density will be
68025.sol:
Maximum percentage error in density is determined by error propagation for a multiplicative relation. Density $\rho = m / L^{3}$, so $\rho = m^{1} L^{-3}$.

For $Z = A^{x} B^{y}$, the percentage error is $\left|x \frac{\Delta A}{A}\right| \times 100\% + \left|y \frac{\Delta B}{B}\right| \times 100\%$.

Substituting $A = m$, $x = 1$, $B = L$, $y = -3$:

$\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100\% = \left|1 \cdot \frac{\Delta m}{m}\right| \times 100\% + \left|{-3} \cdot \frac{\Delta L}{L}\right| \times 100\% = 4\% + 9\% = 13\%$.

69458.text: One of the following values of inputs $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and C respectively gives output $(\mathrm{Y})$ of the following combination of logic gates as ' 1 ' is
69458.sol:
The circuit's output $Y$ represents the logical AND of input $A$ with the OR of inputs $B$ and $C$, expressed as $Y = A \cdot (B + C)$.

For $Y$ to be $1$, both conditions $A = 1$ and $B + C = 1$ must hold true. The OR condition $B + C = 1$ requires at least one of $B$ or $C$ to be $1$.

Evaluating the options: only choice D, with $A=1$, $B=0$, $C=1$, satisfies both $A = 1$ and $B + C = 1$ since $0 + 1 = 1$, leading to $Y = 1 \cdot 1 = 1$.

The correct input combination is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

71253.subject: Biology
71253.text: Part of gene that is transcribed but NOT translated is __________.
71253.sol:
In eukaryotes, the structural gene is split into coding sequences called exons and non-coding intervening sequences called introns.

During transcription, both exons and introns are transcribed to form the primary transcript (hnRNA).

During post-transcriptional modification (splicing), the introns are removed and the exons are joined together to form mature mRNA.

The mature mRNA is then translated into a protein. Therefore, introns are the parts of a gene that are transcribed but not translated.

Answer: intron

71258.subject: Biology
71258.text: Wobble hypothesis explains which one of the following properties of genetic code?
71258.sol:
The Wobble hypothesis, proposed by Francis Crick, explains the degeneracy of the genetic code. It states that the third base of a codon can form non-standard base pairs with the first base of the anticodon on the tRNA. This flexibility (wobble) allows a single tRNA molecule to recognize and bind to more than one codon, which explains why multiple codons can code for the same amino acid (degeneracy).

Answer: Degeneracy of genetic code.

71703.subject: Chemistry
71703.text: Which orbital overlap produces a $\sigma$ bond in HCl?
71703.sol:
The electronic configuration of H is $1s^1$.

The electronic configuration of Cl is $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5$.

The unpaired electron in the hydrogen atom is present in the $1s$ orbital, which is spherically symmetrical.

The unpaired electron in the chlorine atom is present in one of the $3p$ orbitals, which is dumbbell-shaped.

The formation of the HCl molecule involves the axial overlap of the half-filled $1s$ orbital of the hydrogen atom with the half-filled $3p$ orbital of the chlorine atom.

This head-on overlap between an $s$ orbital and a $p$ orbital results in the formation of a $\sigma$ bond.

Thus, the orbital overlap that produces a $\sigma$ bond in HCl is $s-p$.

Answer: s$-$p

72119.text: A parallel plate capacitor with capacitance $1\ \mu\text{F}$ is being charged at a rate such that the potential difference across it changes at $10^6\ \text{V/s}$. The instantaneous displacement current between the plates is
72119.sol:
The displacement current $I_d$ between the plates of a capacitor is given by

$I_d = \varepsilon_0 \dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$

Since the electric flux $\Phi_E = EA = \dfrac{V}{d}A$, we have

$I_d = \varepsilon_0 \dfrac{A}{d} \dfrac{dV}{dt} = C \dfrac{dV}{dt}$

Given $C = 1\ \mu\text{F} = 10^{-6}\ \text{F}$ and $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 10^6\ \text{V/s}$

$I_d = 10^{-6} \times 10^6 = 1\ \text{A}$

Answer: $1\ \text{A}$

72361.subject: Physics
72361.text: $Light enters from air into water of refractive index \dfrac{4}{3}$. The percentage change in its wavelength is
72361.sol:
The wavelength of light in a medium of refractive index $\mu$ is given by $\lambda' = \dfrac{\lambda}{\mu}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength in air.

Given $\mu = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

$\lambda' = \dfrac{\lambda}{4/3} = \dfrac{3\lambda}{4}$

Change in wavelength, $\Delta \lambda = \lambda - \lambda' = \lambda - \dfrac{3\lambda}{4} = \dfrac{\lambda}{4}$

Percentage change in wavelength $= \dfrac{\Delta \lambda}{\lambda} \times 100 = \dfrac{\lambda/4}{\lambda} \times 100 = 25\%$

Answer: $25\ \%$

72382.text: The logic gate equivalent to given logic gate is
72382.sol:
The inputs $A$ and $B$ are passed through NOT gates, giving outputs $\bar{A}$ and $\bar{B}$.

These outputs are fed into a NOR gate. The Boolean expression for the final output $Y$ is:

$Y = \overline{\bar{A} + \bar{B}}$

Using De Morgan's theorem, $\overline{X + Y} = \bar{X} \cdot \bar{Y}$:

$Y = \overline{\bar{A}} \cdot \overline{\bar{B}}$

$Y = A \cdot B$

This represents the Boolean expression for an AND gate.

Answer: AND Gate

According to the Geo-scientists, the shape of the earth is:
1. round
2. spherical
3. close to that of a sphere
4. an oblate ellipsoid Select the correct answer using the code given below:
75862.sol: The simplest model for the shape of the entire Earth is a sphere. The Earth's radius is the distance from Earth's center to its surface, about 6,371 kilometers (3,959 $\mathrm{mi} ). Earth is only approximately spherical, so no single value serves as its natural radius. Since the Earth is flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator, geodesy represents the shape of the earth with an oblate spheroid. The oblate spheroid, or oblate ellipsoid, is an ellipsoid of revolution obtained by rotating an ellipse about its shorter axis.$

77848.subject: Mathematics
77848.text:
Passage: A 4-digit number is selected at random formed by using the digits $0$, $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$ (where repetition of digits is not allowed).

Question: What is the probability that the number selected is divisible by $3$ ?
77848.sol:
Total number of $4$-digit numbers formed using $0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ without repetition:

The thousands place can be filled in $4$ ways (excluding $0$).

The remaining $3$ places can be filled in ^{4}P_{3} = 24$ ways.

Total possible numbers $= 4 \times 24 = 96$.

A number is divisible by 3$ if the sum of its digits is a multiple of $3$.

The sum of all given digits is $0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10$.

To choose $4$ digits whose sum is a multiple of $3$, the excluded digit must leave a remainder of $1$ when divided by $3$. Thus, the excluded digit can be $1$ or $4$.

Case 1: Excluding $1$, the digits are $0, 2, 3, 4$.

Number of $4$-digit numbers $= 3 \times 3! = 18$.

Case 2: Excluding $4$, the digits are $0, 1, 2, 3$.

Number of $4$-digit numbers $= 3 \times 3! = 18$.

Total favorable outcomes $= 18 + 18 = 36$.

Required probability $= \dfrac{36}{96} = \dfrac{3}{8}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{8}$

78584.text: Paragraph: Read the following information and answer: Consider the following statements : 1. Modal value of the marks in Physics lies in the interval $30-40$. 2. Median of the marks in Physics is less than that of marks in Mathematics. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
78584.sol:
(1) Modal value of the marks of Physics is the interval in which maximum number of students got his marks. In the marks interval of ( $30-40)$, number of students in Physics is 30 , which is largest number of students in any interval. Hence, modal values of marks in Physics is (30-40). Statement (1) is correct.
(2) Median class is given by $\left(\frac{N}{2}\right)^{\text{th }}$ item i.e. $\left(\frac{100}{2}\right)^{\text{th }}$ item which is 50th item. This corresponds to the class interval of $(40-50)$ for Physics and $(30-40)$ for Mathematics.

$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Medium }=l_1+\frac{\frac{N}{2}-C . f .}{f} \times i \\ & \therefore \text{ Median for Physics }=40+\frac{\frac{100}{2}-49}{26} \times 10\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =40+\frac{50-49}{26} \times 10=40.385 \\ & \text{Median for Maths }=30+\frac{\frac{100}{2}-31}{38} \times 10 \\ & =30+\frac{50-31}{38} \times 10=35\end{aligned}$
Thus, median of the marks in Physics is more than median of the marks in Mathematics.
Hence, statement (2) is not correct.

82229.subject: Physics
82229.text: The radius of the first permitted Bohr orbit for the electron, in a hydrogen atom equals $0.51 Å$ and its ground state energy equals $-13.6 \mathrm{eV}$. If the electron in the hydrogen atom is replaced by muon $\left(\mu^{-1}\right)$ [Charge same as electron and mass $207 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}$ ], the first Bohr radius and ground state energy will be
82229.sol:
Key Idea Hydrogen atom can be considered to be the system of two charges, positive charged nucleus and negative charged electron. A system of this kind is equivalent to a single particle of mass $m^{\prime}$ that revolves around the position of the heavier particle. Then, the reduced mass of electron is
$$
m^{\prime}=\frac{m M}{m+M}
$$
where, $m=$ mass of electron and
$$
M=\text{ mass of nucleus }
$$
Its values is less than $m$.





Given, radius of first orbit for electron $\mathrm{r}_1=0.51 Å$, ground state energy of electron, $\mathrm{E}_1=-13.6 \mathrm{eV}$, mass of electron $=\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}}$ mass of muon, $\mathrm{m}_\mu=207 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}$ and mass of nucleus, $M=1836 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}$ When electron in hydrogen atom is replaced by muon, the reduced mass of muon is
$$
\mathrm{m}_\mu^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_\mu \mathrm{M}}{\mathrm{m}_\mu+\mathrm{M}}
$$


Substituting the given values in Eq. (i), we get
$$
\mathrm{m}_\mu^{\prime}=\frac{207 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}} \times 1836 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}}{207 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}+1836 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}} \approx 186 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}}
$$
The radius of first orbit in hydrogen atom for electron is given by,
$$
\mathrm{r}_1=\frac{\mathrm{h}^2 \varepsilon_0}{\pi \mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{e}^2}
$$
The radius of first orbit for muon is
$$
\mathrm{r}_1^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{h}^2 \varepsilon_0}{\pi \mathrm{m}_\mu^{\prime} \mathrm{e}^2}
 
\begin{aligned}
& {\left[\because \text{ charge of } \mu=\text{ charge of } \mathrm{e}^{-}\right]} \\
& =\frac{\mathrm{h}^2 \varepsilon_0}{\pi \times 186 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{e}^2} \\
& =\left(\frac{\mathrm{h}^2 \varepsilon_0}{\pi \mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{e}} \mathrm{e}^2}\right) \frac{\mathrm{l}}{186}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_1}{186} \\
& =\frac{0.51}{186} Å \quad\left[\because \mathrm{r}_1=0.51 Å\right] \\
& =2.74 \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~m} \quad\left[\because 1 Å=10^{-10} \mathrm{~m}\right] \\
&
\end{aligned}
$$
The total energy of electron is given by
$$
\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{-\mathrm{mZ}^2 \mathrm{e}^4}{8 \varepsilon_0^2 \mathrm{~h}^2}\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}^2}\right) \Rightarrow \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{n}} \propto \mathrm{m}
$$
For electron in first orbit of hydrogen atom,
$$
\mathrm{E}_1=\mathrm{km}_{\mathrm{e}}
$$
where, $\mathrm{k}=\frac{\mathrm{e}^4}{8 \varepsilon_0^2 \mathrm{~h}^2}=$ constant.

For muon in first orbit
$ \begin{array}{rlr}
\mathrm{E}_1{ }^{\prime} & =\mathrm{km}_\mu{ }^{\prime} & \\
& =\mathrm{k} \times 186 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{e}} & \text{ [from Eq. (i)] } \\
& =186 \mathrm{~km}_{\mathrm{e}} & \\
& =186 \mathrm{E}_1 & \text{ [from Eq. (iv)] } \\
& =186(-13.6) \mathrm{eV} & \text{ (given) } \\
& =-2529.6 \mathrm{eV} & \\
& =-2.5 \mathrm{keV} &
\end{array}  \therefore$ The values are closest to that of options (3).

$= \dfrac{2B}{{\mu}_{0}}\dfrac{A\dfrac{3}{2}}{\sqrt{\pi}}$

$⇒ n = 2$ and $m = 1 . 5$

$∴ n + m = 3 . 5$

Now for small lamina

So moment of Inertia of remaining part

95880.sol:
In the five-kingdom classification system, the kingdom Monera includes all the prokaryotic celled organisms. Prokaryotes are organisms whose cells lack a well-defined nucleus. All the bacterial groups are included in Monera as well since bacteria have a prokaryotic cell structure. Cyanobacteria are a group of free-living photosynthetic bacteria that perform oxygenic photosynthetic process which are included in the kingdom Monera. Bacillus is a genus of rod-shaped bacteria under Monera. Oscillatoria is a group of cyanobacteria which reproduces by fragmentation method.

Kingdom Protista includes all single-celled eukaryotes. Protozoans, Euglenoids, Dinoflagellates are included in this group. Organisms in the kingdom are primarily aquatic and some show presence of flagella and cilia. Euglena and Trypanosoma come under the kingdom Protista.

All the chlorophyll containing eukaryotes are included in the kingdom Plantae. All the organisms in it have cell wall made of cellulose and are autotrophic (some partial autotrophic- insectivorous plant). It also includes the thallophytes like algae group Chlamydomonas. Solanum is an economically important plant genus which includes potato and tomato.

Fungi form a unique group of heterotrophic organisms showing wide diversity. These organisms have cell wall which is made of chitin unlike cellulose seen in plants. The commonly consumed mushroom and toadstool are included in this kingdom. These organisms are achlorophyllous as they are all non-photosynthetic. Penicillium and Mucor are part of the Fungi.

Kingdom Animalia includes all the multicellular-eukaryotic animals. The organisms are heterotrophic and lack cell walls. Animals digest their food internally showing holozoic nutrition. Majority of them show capacity of locomotion. Felis is a genus of this kingdom which includes small and medium sized cats. Panthera is another genus that includes all spotted cats. It also includes the tiger and lion group.

101058.text: If the linear momentum is increased by $50 \%$, then kinetic energy will increase by
101058.sol:
Kinetic energy of a body, $K=\frac{p^2}{2 m}$ where $p$ is the momentum of the body and $m$ is the mass of the body
$p^{\prime}=p+\frac{50}{100} p=\frac{3}{2} p$
Assuming $m$ remains constant
$\therefore \frac{K^{\prime}}{K}=\left(\frac{p^{\prime}}{p}\right)^2=\frac{9}{4}$
$\%$ increase in kinetic energy $=\frac{K^{\prime}-K}{K} \times 100 \%$
$=\left(\frac{K^{\prime}}{K}-1\right) \times 100 \%=\left(\frac{9}{4}-1\right) \times 100 \%=125 \%$

102436.subject: Physics
102436.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the angular speeds of various rotating bodies.

(A)Second hand of an analog clock(I)$\dfrac{\pi}{43200}$ rad/s
(B)Minute hand of an analog clock(II)$\dfrac{\pi}{21600}$ rad/s
(C)Hour hand of an analog clock(III)$\dfrac{\pi}{1800}$ rad/s
(D)Earth's rotation about its own axis(IV)$\dfrac{\pi}{30}$ rad/s

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
102436.sol:
The angular speed of a rotating body is given by $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$, where $T$ is the time period of rotation.

For the second hand of a clock, $T = 60$ s.
$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{60} = \dfrac{\pi}{30}$ rad/s. (A matches IV)

For the minute hand of a clock, $T = 60$ minutes $= 3600$ s.
$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{3600} = \dfrac{\pi}{1800}$ rad/s. (B matches III)

For the hour hand of a clock, $T = 12$ hours $= 12 \times 3600 = 43200$ s.
$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{43200} = \dfrac{\pi}{21600}$ rad/s. (C matches II)

For the Earth's rotation about its own axis, $T = 24$ hours $= 24 \times 3600 = 86400$ s.
$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{86400} = \dfrac{\pi}{43200}$ rad/s. (D matches I)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

102875.subject: Physics
102875.text: An electric dipole of length $8\text{ cm}$ consists of two equal and opposite charges $+q$ and $-q$. The electric potential at a point on the axial line, which is closer to the positive charge, is given as $\dfrac{8}{9}Kq \times 10^2\text{ V}$ (where $K = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}$). The distance of this point from the centre of the dipole is:
102875.sol:
Let the distance of the point from the centre of the dipole be $r$.

The exact formula for the electric potential on the axial line of a dipole (closer to $+q$) is:
$V = \dfrac{K(q \times 2a)}{r^2 - a^2}$

Given length of the dipole, $2a = 8\text{ cm} \Rightarrow a = 4\text{ cm}$.
Converting distances to metres, $2a = 8 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}$ and $r^2 - a^2 = (r^2 - 16) \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2$ (where $r$ is in cm).

Substituting the given values:
$V = \dfrac{K \times q \times 8 \times 10^{-2}}{(r^2 - 16) \times 10^{-4}} = \dfrac{800Kq}{r^2 - 16}$

We are given that $V = \dfrac{8}{9}Kq \times 10^2 = \dfrac{800Kq}{9}$.

Equating the two expressions:
$\dfrac{800Kq}{r^2 - 16} = \dfrac{800Kq}{9}$

$r^2 - 16 = 9$
$r^2 = 25 \Rightarrow r = 5\text{ cm}$

Note: Using the short dipole approximation ($V = \dfrac{Kp}{r^2}$) would incorrectly yield $r = 3\text{ cm}$.

Answer: $5\text{ cm}$

103902.subject: Physics
103902.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a decreasing current flows from point A to point B through an ideal inductor, the electric potential at point A is lower than the electric potential at point B ($V_A < V_B$).

Reason (R): According to Lenz's law, the induced emf opposes the decrease in current, making the inductor act as a source with its positive terminal towards point B.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
103902.sol:
When current flows from A to B, the potential difference equation is $V_A - L\dfrac{di}{dt} = V_B$.

Since the current is decreasing, $\dfrac{di}{dt}$ is negative. Therefore, the term $-L\dfrac{di}{dt}$ becomes positive, which means $V_A + \text{positive value} = V_B$. This implies $V_A < V_B$, making the Assertion true.

According to Lenz's law, the induced emf opposes the change in current. To oppose a decrease, the inductor attempts to maintain the current flow in the same direction (from A to B). To drive current from A to B, it must act like a battery with its positive terminal at B and negative terminal at A. Thus, the Reason is true and correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

103950.subject: Physics
103950.text: A conducting loop of resistance $R$ is placed in a uniform, constant magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to its plane. The area of the loop is continuously increased from an initial value $A_0$ at $t=0$ in such a way that the electrical power dissipated in the loop remains a constant value $P_0$. Which of the following expressions represents the area of the loop as a function of time $t$?
103950.sol:
The power dissipated in the loop is given by $P = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R}$, where $\varepsilon$ is the induced EMF.

Given that the power is a constant $P_0$, we have:
$P_0 = \dfrac{\varepsilon^2}{R} \implies |\varepsilon| = \sqrt{P_0 R}$

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of the induced EMF is:
$|\varepsilon| = \left| \dfrac{d\Phi}{dt} \right| = B \dfrac{dA}{dt}$ (since $B$ is constant and perpendicular to the loop)

Equating the two expressions for $|\varepsilon|$:
$B \dfrac{dA}{dt} = \sqrt{P_0 R} \implies \dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B}$

Integrating with respect to time $t$, with the initial condition $A(0) = A_0$:
$\int_{A_0}^{A} dA = \int_{0}^{t} \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B} dt$
$A(t) - A_0 = \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B} t$
$A(t) = A_0 + \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B} t$

Answer: $A(t) = A_0 + \dfrac{\sqrt{P_0 R}}{B} t$

104119.subject: Physics
104119.text: A series LCR circuit with inductance $10 \text{ mH}$, capacitance $100 \text{ \mu F}$, and resistance $50 \text{ \Omega}$ is connected to an AC source of voltage $V = 100\sqrt{2} \sin(1000t)$ volt. The RMS current and the power factor of the circuit are respectively:
104119.sol:
From the given voltage equation $V = 100\sqrt{2} \sin(1000t)$, the peak voltage is $V_0 = 100\sqrt{2} \text{ V}$ and the angular frequency is $\omega = 1000 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

The RMS voltage is $V_{rms} = \dfrac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}} = 100 \text{ V}$.

The resonant angular frequency of the circuit is:

$\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10 \times 10^{-3} \times 100 \times 10^{-6}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-6}}} = 1000 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$

Since $\omega = \omega_0$, the circuit is in resonance. At resonance, the impedance $Z$ is equal to the resistance $R$ ($Z = 50 \text{ \Omega}$) and the phase difference between voltage and current is zero.

The power factor is $\cos \phi = \cos(0) = 1$.

The RMS current is $I_{rms} = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z} = \dfrac{100}{50} = 2 \text{ A}$.

Answer: $2 \text{ A}, 1$

104257.subject: Physics
104257.text:
The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum is given by:
$\vec{B} = 2 \times 10^{-8} \sin(0.5 \times 10^3 x + 1.5 \times 10^{11} t) \hat{j}$ T

Which of the following represents the corresponding vector equation for the electric field?
104257.sol:
The phase of the wave is $(kx + \omega t)$. Since both the $x$ term and the $t$ term have the same positive sign, the wave is propagating in the negative $x$-direction ($-\hat{i}$).

The direction of propagation is given by the cross product $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.
We know the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ oscillates along the $+\hat{j}$ direction.
Let the direction of the electric field be $\hat{n}$.
$\hat{n} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}$
Since $\hat{k} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}$, the electric field must oscillate along the $+\hat{k}$ direction.

The amplitude of the electric field $E_0$ is related to the magnetic field amplitude $B_0$ by:
$E_0 = c B_0 = (3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}) \times (2 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T}) = 6 \text{ V/m}$

Combining the amplitude, phase, and direction, the electric field equation is:
$\vec{E} = 6 \sin(0.5 \times 10^3 x + 1.5 \times 10^{11} t) \hat{k} \text{ V/m}$

Answer: $6 \sin(0.5 \times 10^3 x + 1.5 \times 10^{11} t) \hat{k}$ V/m

104897.text: Ratio of longest wavelengths corresponding to Lyman and Balmer series in hydrogen spectrum is
104897.sol:
The transition equation for Lyman series is given by
$\frac{1}{\lambda}=R\left(\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{n^2}\right)$
for largest wavelength, $n=2$.
$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{\lambda_{\max }}=R\left(\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}\right)$
The transition equation for Balmer series is given by
$\frac{1}{\lambda}=R\left(\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{n^2}\right)$
for largest wavelength, $n = 3$
$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{\lambda_{\max }}=R\left(\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{3^2}\right)$
Therefore, $\frac{\lambda_{L_{\max }}}{\lambda_{B_{\max }}}=\frac{\left(\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{3^2}\right)}{\left(\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}\right)}=\frac{\frac{5}{36}}{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{5}{27}$

111939.subject: Chemistry
111939.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The carbocation $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\mathrm{C}-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3$ is less stable than $\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$.

Reason (R): The $+I$ effect of a tert-butyl group is greater than that of an ethyl group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
111939.sol:
Assertion (A) is true because the stability of alkyl carbocations is primarily determined by hyperconjugation, which depends on the number of $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms. The carbocation $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3\mathrm{C}-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_3$ has only 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens (from the right methyl group; the tert-butyl group has no $\alpha$-hydrogens). The carbocation $\mathrm{CH}_3-\stackrel{\oplus}{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$ has 5 $\alpha$-hydrogens (3 from the left methyl group and 2 from the right methylene group). More $\alpha$-hydrogens result in more hyperconjugative structures, making the latter more stable.

Reason (R) is true because a tert-butyl group has three electron-donating methyl groups, making its $+I$ effect stronger than that of an ethyl group.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). If the $+I$ effect were the dominant factor, the first carbocation would be more stable. The actual reason for the higher stability of the second carbocation is the dominance of hyperconjugation over the inductive effect.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

112629.subject: Chemistry
112629.text: An alkane with the molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}$ undergoes oxidation when treated with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ to yield an alcohol. What is the IUPAC name of the alcohol formed?
112629.sol:
The given molecular formula is $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}$, which corresponds to an alkane. The possible structural isomers for $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}$ are:
1) $n$-Pentane ($\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$)
2) 2-Methylbutane ($\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$)
3) 2,2-Dimethylpropane ($\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_3)_4$)

Alkanes generally resist oxidation. However, an alkane having a tertiary hydrogen atom can be selectively oxidized to the corresponding alcohol by strong oxidizing agents like $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$.

Among the isomers of $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}$, only 2-Methylbutane possesses a tertiary hydrogen atom (at C-2). Therefore, it is the isomer that will undergo oxidation.

The oxidation reaction replaces the tertiary hydrogen with a hydroxyl ($-\mathrm{OH}$) group:
$\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{KMnO}_4} \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}_3)-\mathrm{CH}_2-\mathrm{CH}_3$

The resulting product is 2-Methylbutan-2-ol.

Answer: 2-Methylbutan-2-ol

113923.text: A solution containing approximately $68\%$ nitric acid and $32\%$ water by mass is prepared. Which of the following correctly describes the type of deviation this mixture shows from Raoult's law and the type of azeotrope it forms?
options: Negative deviation and Maximum boiling azeotrope
Positive deviation and Minimum boiling azeotrope
Negative deviation and Minimum boiling azeotrope
Positive deviation and Maximum boiling azeotrope
113923.sol:
When nitric acid and water are mixed, the new intermolecular interactions (A-B) between nitric acid and water molecules are stronger than the interactions in the pure components (A-A and B-B) due to strong hydrogen bonding.

As a result, the escaping tendency of molecules decreases, leading to a lower vapour pressure than expected from Raoult's law. This is called a negative deviation.

Because the vapour pressure is lowered, the solution must be heated to a higher temperature to boil. Thus, at a specific composition (approximately $68\%$ $\text{HNO}_3$ by mass), it forms a maximum boiling azeotrope.

Answer: Negative deviation and Maximum boiling azeotrope

113969.text: Which one of the following electrolytes has the same value of van't Hoff factor (i) as that of $\mathrm{K}_4\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]$ ?
113969.sol:
The value of van't Hoff factor of the given molecule is as follows :
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Al}_2\left(\mathrm{SO}_4\right)_3 & \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}, \mathrm{i}=5 \\ \mathrm{~K}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 & \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{~K}^{+}+\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}, \mathrm{i}=3 \\ \mathrm{~K}_3\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right] & \rightleftharpoons 3 \mathrm{~K}^{+}+\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]^{3+}, \mathrm{i}=4 \\ \mathrm{Al}\left(\mathrm{NO}_3\right)_3 & \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{NO}_3^{-}, \mathrm{i}=4\end{aligned}$
The van't Hoff factor for $\mathrm{K}_4\left[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6\right]$ is
